subject: Proposal: 3-year prepay + ramp schedule — Acme Corp
messages:
From: Karen Li <karen.li@acme.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Hargrove <tom.h@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring annual prepay for forecasted usage

Markus —

Thanks for the run-through last week. The execs want to move from our current monthly plan to a prepaid model for 2026 to lock in unit cost, but we need clarity on:

- Incremental discounts for a 3-year commit vs 1-year.
- How billing and reporting will look if our usage ramps (Q1 small, Q2+ larger).
- Any concession for early termination or missed usage minimums.

Can you share a proposed term sheet and a suggested ramp schedule we can show finance? We have a Feb–Mar procurement window and would like rough numbers by next week.

Appreciate it —
Karen Li
Director, Cloud Platform
Acme Corp

From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Karen Li <karen.li@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual prepay for forecasted usage

Karen —

Thanks for the clear list. I pushed a quick draft term sheet to the team this morning and we assembled a recommended ramp that aligns discounts to committed spend bands. High level:

- 1-year prepay: 18% off list
- 3-year prepay: 28% off list, with a built-in annual step-down if usage materially exceeds forecast (protects Acme vs overcommit)
- Ramp schedule: conservative Q1 (30% of committed), Q2 (60%), Q3–Q4 (100% steady-state). We can make the ramp more front-loaded if needed.

I attached a working term sheet and an XLS with a few ramp permutations for finance to model. Quick asks: which internal chargeback date does finance use (calendar vs fiscal) and do you require SLA credits written into the contract? Those answers influence the concession we can offer.

Next step: I propose a short call Friday to walk the term sheet; I can include Lauren to cover billing mechanics and Aditya to speak to SLA/training credits.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: Redwood_TermSheet_Acme_3yr_v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
             prepay-ramp-schedule.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)

From: Tom Hargrove <tom.h@acme.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Karen Li <karen.li@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual prepay for forecasted usage

Markus —

Couple of clarifying points from procurement and finance:

1) Finance asked whether the 3-year discount (28%) can be applied as a blended effective rate if we commit to a ramp (i.e., year 1 lower usage, we still realize a blended lower cost across term).
2) Procurement pushed back on the early termination clause — they want a softer exit (pro rata refund for unused prepay) or a one-time buyout option, instead of the standard forfeiture.
3) We need explicit language around audit logs and data retention tied to regulatory audit cycles; is that a feasible add-on?

If you can reflect these in a v2, we can move to legal review. Friday call is fine.

Thanks — Tom
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corp

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hargrove <tom.h@acme.com>, Karen Li <karen.li@acme.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual prepay for forecasted usage

Tom / Karen —

Appreciate the concrete asks. Quick responses before our call:

- Blended effective rate: yes — we can present the 3-year as a committed spend bucket with an annual true-up that yields a blended effective per-token/unit rate. I attached a conservative example in the XLS (tab: blended-example).
- Early termination: we can offer a pro rata refund less a 10% administrative charge if termination happens after year 1; for terminations in year 1, standard buyout (50% of remaining committed value) applies. We can flex that in negotiation but that's our starting point.
- Audit logs/data retention: Redwood Private customers can set retention windows and export audit logs; we can add a contract SLA that includes quarterly evidence exports for regulated audits. That will require a Private deployment addendum if you want on-prem retention.

On Friday I'll walk through billing flow (how prepay invoices are issued and how we show consumption on the console) and Aditya will cover SLA credits. If Friday works at 10:00 PT I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karen Li <karen.li@acme.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Hargrove <tom.h@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual prepay for forecasted usage

Lauren / Markus —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the attachments — those examples helped. Procurement is comfortable proceeding to legal review if Redwood can commit to the following changes in the term sheet:

- Blended effective rate language and the annual true-up mechanism included in the main contract (not just the SOW).
- Early termination pro rata refund (after year 1) with the 10% admin fee as proposed.
- Add a short Private addendum option that we can evaluate (not required at signature).
- Inclusion of quarterly audit-log exports for the duration of the term.

If you can produce a clean v2 reflecting those bullets and drop the DocuSign link, we can route to our legal team this week. Also want to lock an expected start/billing date: target Go-Live July 1 so finance can map to FY26 budgets.

If that all looks reasonable we can move forward.

Best,
Karen Li
Director, Cloud Platform
Acme Corp
